note: Style plate: every Gallic War picture uses this as its style reference.
style: A Roman history painting in the manner of Jean-Léon Gérôme and Lawrence Alma-Tadema: crisp academic realism, brilliant Mediterranean daylight, clear warm light and deep blue shadow, precise archaeological detail of 58 BC, rich painterly finish. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, lettering, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: A Roman legion of 58 BC on the march through a wide sunlit valley in Gaul: a long column of legionaries in mail shirts (lorica hamata) with oval-topped curved rectangular shields, bronze Montefortino helmets with cheek-guards, javelins (pila) on their shoulders, the eagle standard and red vexilla at the head, mounted officers, mule trains, and beyond them green hills, a river and blue mountains under towering white clouds. Wide view; figures small.
